DEVICE: the repository controls a scanning SQUID microscope; a physical microscope is a Microscope or a subclass such as SusceptometerMicroscope (docs/pages/microscope.rst:4), the class the documented examples construct with the repository's scanning-squid directory on the path (workflow.rst:15). The routing override MHS/registry/overrides/p3-reauthor-routing.json makes microscope.susceptometer:SusceptometerMicroscope (susceptometer.py:51) the card's entry, replacing the untriaged recon route; G7 resolves it at the pin. DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: a decorated direct Driver, not the PythonObjectDriver helper. SCOPE: of the microscope's two ways of moving the SQUID, only the Attocube coarse positioners have a stop (atto.stop: 'stop n', then mode gnd, atto.py:143-152); the piezo scanner's goto writes a ramp to an analog-output task created and awaited inside the call (scanner.py:159-168), which nothing outside can stop, so scanner motion, touchdowns, approach, surfaces and scans are not served. Served: atto_step (atto.step, then the mode read back; if atto.step raises, the axis is stopped and grounded with atto.stop, its mode read back, and the outcome is unknown), atto_ground (the safe-state action) and the e-stop (atto.stop for z, x, y, every axis tried, then every mode read back with getm; success only if all read gnd), and reads of the scanner position (get_pos, NI-DAQ, clamped by the upstream to the configured limits) and of the three axis modes (refused BUSY during a step). R2: a wrong step can crash the SQUID into the sample (workflow.rst:34-38, 54). LIMITS: steps is operator_required; the example overlay allows -20 to 20 requested steps per command. STEP COUNT: the limit bounds the count requested, not the steps made. step sends its stepu or stepd command with ask (atto.py:168-169), and the class's ask_raw, which QCoDeS's ask calls, writes every command twice and checks the second reply for ERROR (atto.py:109-124). The source does not show what the ANC300 does with the second copy: possibly the steps again (up to about twice the count; the wait of atto.py:172 covers one count, so the gnd of atto.py:173 may cut the second run short), a restarted count, or ERROR, after which step raises with the first copy under way. The operator measures the steps one command makes on the bench before setting the limit. KNOWN LIMITS OF THE STOP: the upstream holds no lock on the ANC300 VISA session, so an e-stop landing while step exchanges its first commands may interleave with them (the read-back then fails; the latch is kept and the stop retried); step, waking after the e-stop, grounds the axis again and records the full requested move in its metadata (atto.py:173-176). A step checks for cancellation under the lock the stop takes before it starts, and a stop that runs while a step is in flight reports itself unconfirmed (the upstream step may set its axis to stp after it, atto.py:167-169); the runtime keeps the latch and re-runs the stop, which confirms once the step has returned (a package case lets a step's commands arrive after the first stop and checks that the confirming re-run stops that axis again). The scanner is not stopped and keeps its voltage. HARDWARE BACKEND: native.connect builds SusceptometerMicroscope(config_file, temp); importing it writes squid_units.txt into the working directory, and construction closes all QCoDeS instruments, creates logs, initialises the ANC300 (frequencies, voltages, every axis grounded; prints to stdout), connects the Lakeshores and lock-ins and MOVES THE SCANNER TO [0, 0, 0] V (scanner.py:61) before the driver serves anything: open it only with the SQUID retracted. 'pip install .' does not work (setup.py names a scanning_squid directory the checkout does not have); the lock gives the README's conda environment. FAKE: atto and scanner stand-ins following atto.py; positions and step bookkeeping are placeholders; the fake does not wait. It writes the step command twice, as upstream, but counts the requested steps once: a placeholder and a gap of the fake, which says nothing about the steps a command makes (a hardware driver's fake view carries the SDK's fixed fake fidelity contract, so the gap is stated here and in fake.py).
